title: Drop and screen on the counter
titleKid: Run back in front of your defenders
brief: We have the ball in their half. Watch what happens next.
briefKid: We have the ball near their goal. Watch what happens.
question: They have won it and are breaking past you. Where do you go?
questionKid: They won the ball and attack. Where do you go?

takeaway.standard: If the counter has already gone past you, don't chase the ball: drop into the middle in front of your centre-backs and slow the attack until help arrives.
takeaway.kid: If you can't catch the ball, run back in front of your defenders.

misconceptions.text: You chased the ball from behind; you won't catch it, and now nobody is screening in front of your centre-backs.
misconceptions.textKid: You can't catch the ball from behind, so run back into the middle.

misconceptions.text: You dropped all the way into your back line, so the space in front of it is free for them to play into.
misconceptions.textKid: You are too far back. Stay a few steps in front of your defenders.

notes: The #8 who gave the ball away (us-RCM) is keyed to back off 2-4 m goal-side of the carrier, so they are the first defender delaying the counter (T2), and the #9 is keyed to trail the break at up to 7.5 m/s. Left automatic, the #9 raced 22 m in 2.2 s (peak 11.8 m/s) past the dribbler and pressed from the front, so the #6 was judged as covering the #9, which contradicted the brief. The ideal moved 1 m to the engine's (49, 40).
